faq.q: Do zebra stripes keep flies away?
faq.a: Experiments suggest so. When horses wore striped coats, horseflies approached them but rarely landed, apparently confused as they came in close. Zebras also live where flies spread deadly diseases.
asks: Why would zebras need protection from flies?

faq.a: Some scientists suggested black and white stripes heat differently and stir little breezes. Studies measuring striped and plain barrels or animals found little or no cooling difference, so this idea has weak support.
asks: Are zebras cooler because of stripes?

faq.a: The idea is called motion dazzle: a moving herd of stripes might make it hard to pick one zebra. But lions catch zebras often, and studies suggest lions see stripes poorly from afar, so evidence is thin.
asks: Do stripes help zebras hide from lions?

faq.q: Is every zebra's stripe pattern different?
faq.a: Yes. Like fingerprints, no two zebras have the same stripes. Scientists use photos of stripe patterns to identify individual zebras, and foals may learn their mother's pattern.
asks: Do zebras recognise each other by stripes?

faq.q: Is a zebra white with black stripes or black with white stripes?
faq.a: Zebras have black skin, and the stripes come from cells that make dark pigment in some hairs and not others. So many scientists describe zebras as black with white stripes.
asks: What colour is a zebra underneath?

facts: In a 2019 study, horseflies landed far less often on horses wearing striped coats than on plain ones.
Every zebra has a unique stripe pattern.
